documents.abstract: Unsafe behaviours among hydropower station personnel contribute to accidents and are closely associated with ergonomic risks. To address inefficient manual monitoring and limited consideration of behavioural risks in safety management, this study proposes an improved YOLOv11n-based method for unsafe behaviour detection and develops an ergonomic risk assessment framework using detection results. The method incorporates PConv, an attention mechanism, and Focal Loss into YOLOv11n and integrates YOLOv11n-Pose and DCNN-SE modules to identify unsafe behaviours involving personal protection and actions. Experimental results demonstrate improvements over the comparison model in precision, recall, mean average precision, and inference speed, with robustness to complex backgrounds, small targets, and partial occlusion.

This article examines what effects the use of learning machines may have on human imagination and learning. The narrative of Perseus and Medusa, revisited by Ítalo Calvino, is the image that guides the inquiry: when confronting the Gorgon, the shield protects the gaze and, at the same time, offers an indirect form of approach. From this image, we ask whether generative artificial intelligence tends to petrify thought — by offering answers that precede the effort of creation — or whether it can function as a mediation that broadens perspectives. This is a qualitative, bibliographical and exploratory study, conducted as a theoretical essay of philosophical-educational interpretation. The discussion articulates lightness and visibility in Calvino, Nietzsche's critique of education subordinated to haste and utility, the notion of symbolic forms in Cassirer, and Maxine Greene's educational imagination. The analysis shows that technology does not determine, by itself, either the impoverishment or the expansion of imagination. The risk arises when the automated response takes the place of the student's questioning, hesitation and elaboration. We conclude that artificial intelligence can serve learning when it remains as a shield: a questioned, limited mediation subordinated to human authorship.

Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly deployed in consequential settings, network diagnostics, clinical reasoning, financial oracles, robotic control, yet their failure modes remain poorly characterised at the system level. This paper advances a candidate structural reading: that degradation in multi-agent LLM systems is not primarily a function of individual model quality but emerges from the interaction of four compounding mechanisms operating across the coordination stack. We identify these as (1) entropy accumulation from intrinsic agent properties that grow monotonically with interaction rounds, (2) communication inefficiency arising from redundant token generation and poorly structured information exchange, (3) deliberation pathology in which consensus mechanisms propagate rather than correct errors, and (4) censored feedback that prevents agents from distinguishing coordination failure from stochastic task failure. Drawing on findings from cs.MA and cs.DC preprints, we argue, as a heuristic reading, not a formal derivation, that these four mechanisms occupy distinct layers of the coordination stack but interact in ways that make system-level degradation substantially harder to diagnose than any single-layer failure. The thesis generates concrete falsification paths: the entropy growth rate α should be measurable and architecture-dependent; communication efficiency gains should be separable from accuracy gains in ablation; deliberation accuracy should correlate negatively with inter-model error correlation; and censored-feedback regret should decompose into structural-search and statistical-monitoring terms with distinct scaling behaviours. We argue that treating these mechanisms as jointly constitutive of a degradation topology, rather than as independent bugs, motivates a candidate class of system-level monitoring primitives. The abstract reports empirical findings from the cited preprints; whether the interaction effects generalise beyond the specific architectures and benchmarks studied is open. All cited papers are arXiv preprints and have not been peer-reviewed; findings should be treated as preliminary. Authorship: Saluca Agentic AI Research Team (Saluca LLC). Large language models (LLMs) are being integrated into clinical environments where deference to authority can cause harm. Following an unsafe instruction represents a distinct safety failure. Whether a brief safety reminder changes this behavior is an important clinical safety question. We evaluated 20 open-weight LLMs across 10,096,800 outputs from 601 instances: 501 synthetic variants derived from 50 templates and 100 MIMIC-IV-derived cases. Each instance was tested across 21 framing cells, four mitigation cells, and ten repetitions. The primary outcome was selection of an overtly or partially unsafe option (A or B). We also measured mapped-category consistency across matched ten-run cells. Here we show that 1.18 million of 10.1 million outputs (11.7%) select a potentially harmful option. Selections decrease from 16.6% without mitigation to 10.1% with mitigation (absolute reduction, 6.5 percentage points; p < 0.001), with reductions in synthetic vignettes (10.6% to 7.2%) and MIMIC-IV-derived cases (46.6% to 24.5%). Potentially harmful option selection decreases in 19 of 20 models. Across 1,009,680 matched ten-run cells, 80.4% return the same response category in all ten repetitions; model-level consistency ranges from 4.4% to 100.0%. Among inconsistent cells, 38.2% vary between potentially harmful and safe categories. A safety reminder reduces, but does not eliminate, potentially harmful option selection across both datasets and 19 of 20 models. Category consistency varies across models. This proof-of-concept study provides an evaluation framework but does not estimate clinical risk in deployed systems. Artificial intelligence models used in the hospital may receive instructions that conflict with patient safety. We tested 20 large language models using synthetic cases and records from real clinical recommendations. Each model chose among two potentially harmful and two safe actions, with or without a short reminder to verify or escalate unsafe requests. Across more than 10 million responses, potentially harmful choices fell from 16.6% without the reminder to 10.1% with it. The reduction occurred in 19 of 20 models. In 80.4% of tests that repeated the same case under the same conditions, a model selected the same type of action in all ten repetitions, with almost no difference with or without the reminder. These experiments show how safety reminders in the instructions given to models and consistency of their choices can be evaluated together. They do not show how often harm would occur in clinical practice.

documents.abstract: Purpose Grounded in cognitive load theory and dual process theory, this study aims to investigate how cognitive complexity and health information literacy (HIL) influence users’ cognitive load, perceived learning and cognitive system utilization when acquiring health-related knowledge through artificial intelligence-generated content (AIGC) and user-generated content (UGC). It aims to reveal cognitive mechanisms underlying these processes and inform improvements in the health information environment. Design/methodology/approach A 2 (learning tools: AIGC vs UGC) × 2 (cognitive complexity: high vs low) × 2 (HIL: high vs low) experimental design was adopted. Data were collected through a questionnaire and evaluated using analysis of variance. Findings Users experienced significant differences in intrinsic and extraneous cognitive load and across all dimensions of perceived learning when using AIGC compared with UGC; Task complexity caused significant differences across all types of cognitive load; HIL levels significantly affected intrinsic and germane cognitive load. Regarding cognitive system utilization, no significant differences emerged between AIGC and UGC. However, higher task complexity increased System 2 engagement universally, and users with higher HIL relied more on System 2 (analytical processing). Originality/value This study develops an integrated framework for examining how learning tools, cognitive complexity and HIL jointly shape learning effectiveness in digital environments. It advances understanding of cognitive processing in digital learning contexts and provides actionable insights for designing cognitively adaptive AIGC and UGC systems.

Exploring Teleoperator Perception through Kinesthetic Feedback Background: Kinesthetic feedback is essential for effective teleoperation, enabling users to perceive and manipulate remote or virtual environments with precision. Haptic codecs exploit human perception thresholds to compress kinesthetic signals, reducing transmission load, but the resulting degradation —together with network-induced delay — may affect both perception and task performance. This work investigates how deadband-based compression and temporal delay jointly influence human performance in teleoperated tasks. Methods: Participants performed two teleoperated tasks under varying levels of deadband compression and network delay. In a letter tracing task, participants traced a reference shape while position and force errors were recorded. In a stiffness discrimination task, participants compared the stiffness of a test spring against soft and stiff reference springs and rated the test stimulus on a four-point scale. Preliminary Results: In the letter tracing task, tracing accuracy declined systematically and monotonically with both increasing compression and increasing delay, with position and force errors rising substantially across the tested parameter range and the largest degradation observed under combined high compression and delay. Degradation was gradual rather than abrupt, with no indication of a threshold beyond which performance broke down. In the stiffness discrimination task, perceived stiffness decreased with increasing delay, consistent with earlier reports. Compression level had no measurable effect on stiffness judgments. Preliminary Conclusion: Kinesthetic codecs enable effective teleoperation under time delay, but performance degrades with increasing compression and delay, and the two tasks showed distinct sensitivity profiles: error-based metrics in a fine motor tracing task were sensitive to both compression and delay, whereas comparative stiffness judgments were sensitive only to delay. These findings suggest that the impact of haptic signal compression and network delay on teleoperator performance is task-dependent, and that codec and network requirements should be tailored to the task at hand.

This study explored the attitudes and experiences of older adults who had used Wearable Physical Activity Monitoring Technology (WPAMT) for at least 30 days, identifying factors influencing continued use and discontinuation. Employing grounded theory, face-to-face interviews with 31 older adults in Hong Kong revealed that most participants held positive attitudes towards WPAMT and a willingness to continue using it. Five determinants largely affected positive attitudes: perceived usefulness, versatility, importance, convenience and effectiveness. Negative attitudes were associated with perceptions of the technology being challenging, unnecessary and unaffordable. Continued use of WPAMT was motivated by utilitarian outcomes, health awareness, trust and the presence of facilitators. Conversely, discontinuation of WPAMT use was associated with technophobia, technological barriers, risk perception and perceived cost.

The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) has impacted various fields, including education. In the context of foreign language (FL) learning, AI tools are increasingly being adopted by both instructors and students to facilitate the teaching and learning processes. This qualitative study explores the utilization of AI tools by English as a Foreign Language (EFL) postgraduate students at the Libyan Academy to enhance their academic writing skills. Data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 10 MA and PhD students in Applied Linguistics and analyzed using thematic analysis. The analysis revealed several key themes: the types of AI tools engaged, perceived benefits, encountered challenges, ethical considerations, and skill development. Findings indicate that students employ a diverse range of AI tools, with levels of dependency varying from limited consultation for specific tasks to heavy reliance for completing various writing assignments. While participants acknowledged significant benefits, particularly in enhancing their writing proficiency, they also reported drawbacks, such as limited access to premium versions of AI applications. The study concludes with recommendations for policymakers, instructors, and students, emphasizing the need for clear institutional guidelines on AI use, initiatives to raise student awareness of its ethical application, and efforts to mitigate challenges that could otherwise passively hinder the development of academic writing skills.

documents.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) technology is a valuable tool to address the evolving needs of young-old adults. This study investigated the factors influencing the adoption of VR technology among young-old adults, extending the technology acceptance model by incorporating trust and perceived risk. Data were collected from 343 respondents aged 60 and above through a structured questionnaire, with structural equation modelling used for data analysis. The findings revealed that trust plays a central role in shaping young-old adults' attitudes towards VR technology and their behavioural intentions to adopt it. Additionally, perceived ease of use and perceived usefulness positively contribute to the formation of trust. Conversely, perceived safety risk and performance risk negatively affect trust.

The development of generative AI (GAI) capabilities has led corporate entities to rethink their strategic initiatives towards sustainable workforce management. This dynamism has been broadly identified as a concern for managerial teams. Despite strong consensus on the roles of organizational human resources and corporate governance in managing the deployment of GAI mechanisms, specific factors contributing to each orientation remain unidentified. The current study addresses this gap by conducting a comprehensive review of factors that may affect sustainability orientation and employee well-being in the context of GAI implementation. The study utilized total interpretive structural modeling (TISM) and cross-impact matrix multiplication applied to the classification (MICMAC) method to develop the hierarchical relationship model. The study identified 16 factors: nine attributed to human resource management (HRM) and seven to the corporate social responsibility (CSR) domain. The study develops an expert-informed structural representation of the interrelationships between the two categories of designated factors. The outcomes identify two foundational factors as independent drivers and one dependent factor related to the social assessment of technology from a CSR perspective. The findings provide a structured interpretation of the interdependence between HRM and CSR factors and their implications for sustainable workforce management and employee health in SMEs. The study offers novel managerial implications on the relative orientations of driving and dependency factors for managing a sustainable workforce while supporting new technology development in the SME context.

Objective This study aimed to evaluate characteristics, first aid and PPE use among patients with occupational corneal foreign body (CFB) injuries.Methods A cross-sectional study included 92 male patients treated at Harran University. Data on demographics, job type, injury cause, PPE use, first aid and occupational safety service exposure were analysed.Results The mean age was 36.04 ± 12.24 years, average work experience 11.86 ± 10.98 years. Welding/metalwork was the most common job (38.0%), and 87.0% of injuries were caused by metallic objects. Treatment delay occurred in 75.0% of patients, incorrect first aid was reported in 9.8%, and 53.3% did not consistently use PPE. Younger patients performed significantly better first aid (p = 0.006), while inconsistent PPE use was significantly higher among those who received occupational health and safety (OHS) services (p = 0.034).Conclusion These findings emphasise the importance of PPE and occupational safety services to reduce eye injury risks in workplaces.

documents.abstract: The study examined the determinants of behavioral intention to use artificial intelligence (AI) among administrative personnel in selected private higher education institutions (HEIs) in Cebu, Philippines, using an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT) framework. The model incorporated trust in AI and AI job insecurity to provide a context-specific understanding of AI adoption in higher education administration. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional research design, data were collected from 243 administrative personnel and analyzed through structural equation modeling. The findings revealed that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and social influence positively and significantly influenced behavioral intention, with social influence demonstrating the strongest relationship. Conversely, facilitating conditions and AI job insecurity did not significantly predict behavioral intention. Trust in AI exhibited a significant negative relationship with behavioral intention, contrary to the hypothesized positive direction. Multigroup analysis further indicated that gender significantly moderated the relationship between performance expectancy and behavioral intention, while institutional tenure moderated the relationship between social influence and behavioral intention. Age did not significantly moderate the relationship between effort expectancy and behavioral intention. The proposedTargeted Administrative Change Management framework provides a foundation for institutional strategies supporting responsible AI adoption, while its effectiveness warrants further empirical validation.

Version 2 cited the CONCAT framework (arXiv:2605.29612) in Section 3.4 and reported its results of up to 2.02x higher efficiency and a 50.1% latency reduction. On 2026-09-22 its authors withdrew the manuscript, writing: "We identified a potential issue in the repeated-run evaluation of our method that may have caused unintended prompt overlap across runs and affected the reported results. We therefore withdraw the manuscript for further investigation and re-evaluation". Those results are removed from the body and the Discussion, and CONCAT is no longer used as evidence; the claim it supported rests, as before, on its two other sources. The Limitations section records the withdrawal. Typographic dashes are removed, mathematical symbols now render in the PDF, and the file carries a neutral name. The abstract below is unchanged apart from punctuation. The problem was found by an automated check and confirmed by hand against arXiv; this version has not had a full claim-by-claim audit. Multi-agent LLM systems are increasingly deployed in settings where individual agent failures can cascade across the collective, yet the mechanisms by which such failures propagate, and the structural conditions under which they are contained or corrected, remain poorly characterised. This paper synthesises seven findings from recent cs.MA and cs.DC preprints to argue a candidate structural pattern (a heuristic reading, not a derivation from a shared formal structure): systemic reliability in multi-agent LLM systems is not primarily a function of individual agent capability, but of the interaction between (a) the topology through which errors can propagate, (b) the credit-assignment mechanisms that identify which components generated the error, and (c) the architectural isolation boundaries that prevent a failure in one execution channel from contaminating others. We argue the analogy by naming specific mechanisms in each case rather than by appeal to a unified formalism. The corpus draws from cs.MA papers on multi-agent deliberation, self-evolution, coordination policy learning, and governance infrastructure, supplemented by cs.DC work on federated orchestration and zero-trust enforcement at physical actuation boundaries. Key findings include: deliberative consensus among LLM agents can degrade accuracy below single-model baselines when high-confidence wrong agents flip correct ones arXiv:2605.30802; architectural channel isolation failures silently block cross-agent memory injection regardless of agent-level correctness arXiv:2606.04896; governance layers at the execution boundary reduce unsafe executions from 88% to near-zero without modifying underlying generators arXiv:2606.04306; and temporal plus structural credit decomposition substantially reduces query complexity in MAS optimisation arXiv:2605.30227. Together these findings suggest that failure propagation and self-correction are topology-dependent phenomena that cannot be addressed by improving agent intelligence alone. Falsification path: if deliberative degradation disappears when inter-agent error correlation is experimentally reduced below 0.3, the error-propagation mechanism is confirmed; if it persists, the topology hypothesis is insufficient and capability variance must be the primary driver. Aim. This paper examines the role of family and faith community in strengthening psychosocial resilience, particularly among young people whose development is negatively affected by the growing use of artificial intelligence (AI) and the prevailing context of post-truth culture. Concept. We proceed from the premise that the quality of family life and family resilience constitute key factors in the healthy intellectual, emotional, and psychosocial development of the individual. We reflect on the contemporary rise of mental health problems among young people within the post-truth context of a media-saturated environment, which emerges as a source of anxiety, weakened critical thinking, and the gradual erosion of emotional (EQ) and social intelligence (SQ). These parameters are projected in a dialectical relationship with the healthy faith community, which holds the potential to create a space of authentic intergenerational belonging, shared values, and social support. Results and Conclusion. The critical analysis develops an original argumentative framework, according to which high-quality family life, family resilience, and participation in healthy faith communities represent a significant dialectic of prevention against the psychosocial risks that current trends in AI use — within the context of post-truth culture — pose to the younger generation: rising anxiety, weakened psychosocial resilience, a limited capacity for deep relational bonds, and a diminished sense of meaning in life. Originality. The paper offers an original interdisciplinary synthesis at the intersection of family psychology, resilience studies, and the spirituality of the contemporary younger generation, providing an applicable model for counselling, pastoral, and educational practice.

Public discourse about Artificial Intelligence (AI) relies on figurative language as a semiotic resource for conceptualising the technology. While previous research has examined metaphor and metonymy in such discourse, less attention has been paid to how these processes interact in shaping figurative construals of AI. Drawing on the Combined Input Hypothesis, this study analyses naturally occurring examples from published blogs and articles as instantiations of two broad types of figurative framings: those positioning the technology in relation to human activity and interaction, and those emerging from debates about its capabilities, risks, and limitations. The findings show that metonymy and metaphor perform distinct but complementary functions. Metonymy foregrounds contextually relevant aspects of AI, while metaphor organises these selected aspects into coherent interpretive configurations, shaping how the technology is construed in terms of its capabilities, relation to human agency, epistemic accessibility, and risks. This interaction gives rise to evaluations ranging from trust and collaboration to scepticism, awe, and fear. The study demonstrates the explanatory value of the Combined Input Hypothesis for understanding how metonymic profiling and metaphorical projection jointly structure figurative discourse about AI.

documents.abstract: Purpose While artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled services have become increasingly prevalent, little is known about how discriminatory service encounters influence consumers’ preference for AI-based service providers. This research aims to investigate whether – and why – perceived discrimination in human service encounters increases consumers’ preference for AI-driven service options. Design/methodology/approach Three studies were conducted to test the proposed framework. Study 1 used an autobiographical recall design, Study 2a experimentally manipulated discrimination, and Study 2b used a 2 × 2 between-subjects experimental design. Mediation and moderated mediation effects were examined using PROCESS. Findings Across the three studies, perceived discrimination was associated with greater preference for AI service providers through reduced social comfort with human providers and enhanced perceptions of AI ethicality. Cultural tightness consistently strengthened the social-comfort pathway, whereas its moderating influence on perceived AI ethicality and the direct effect was less consistent. Practical implications The findings offer actionable insights for designing inclusive service systems, deploying ethical AI solutions and enhancing customer experience strategies. Originality/value This research shows that human–AI service provider preference is shaped not only by the attributes of the available providers but also by consumers’ treatment in a preceding human-delivered service encounter. By linking discriminatory encounters to subsequent provider choice, the study extends research on service encounters, AI-enabled service and service inclusion and offers a socio-psychological explanation for why consumers may develop a stronger preference for AI-based service providers.

documents.abstract: Musculoskeletal trauma may produce persistent functional sequelae that extend beyond anatomical healing and significantly affect occupational participation. This study analyzed the relationship between post-traumatic musculoskeletal impairment, residual functional capacity, occupational demands, work incapacity, return-to-work outcomes, and medico-legal assessment through an integrative review based on the Scientific Method. Evidence from traumatology, rehabilitation medicine, occupational medicine, functional capacity evaluation, and medico-legal literature was examined to identify the principal clinical, functional, psychosocial, and occupational factors associated with delayed or incomplete work reintegration. The findings showed that persistent pain, reduced mobility, muscle weakness, decreased endurance, functional limitations, injury severity, self-efficacy, educational level, physical workload, occupational category, and recovery expectations influence return-to-work trajectories. Functional Capacity Evaluations provide useful objective information regarding work-related performance, but their interpretation requires comparison with actual job demands and integration with clinical, psychosocial, and contextual factors. Workers whose residual functional capacities were compatible with occupational requirements demonstrated more favorable return-to-work outcomes, whereas persistent capacity-demand mismatches were associated with unsuccessful reintegration. Workplace interventions, including modified duties, ergonomic adaptations, coordinated rehabilitation, and graded return-to-work programs, were associated with improved initial and sustained occupational outcomes. From a medico-legal perspective, the evidence supports a clear distinction between anatomical impairment, functional limitation, occupational restriction, and disability. Work capacity should therefore be determined through an interdisciplinary and individualized assessment integrating objective sequelae, functional performance, job-specific requirements, prognosis, rehabilitation potential, and workplace adaptability. This multidimensional framework provides a more precise and defensible basis for disability assessment and for planning safe and sustainable occupational reintegration after musculoskeletal trauma.

This study examines whether firm-initiated generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) communications are associated with firm value in UK-listed tourism, travel, and hospitality (TTH) firms. The final sample includes 177 firms from 2018 to 2024, comprising 68 firms with verified WeChat official accounts and 109 firms retained with zero-valued communication measures. From 105,429 archived posts, we develop a bilingual annotation scheme and supervised deep-learning classifiers to identify GenAI communication and distinguish implementation-salient disclosures from generic mentions. Our preferred measures are share-normalized, capturing both GenAI communication intensity and implementation emphasis relative to total posting activity. Firm- and year-fixed-effects results show that implementation-weighted GenAI communication is positively associated with Tobin's Q and operating performance. Digital innovation partially mediates this relationship, while industry dynamism and complexity strengthen it, but munificence does not. The study contributes a tourism-specific measure of GenAI capability signaling and clarifies the value relevance of implementation-oriented communication in service-intensive digital contexts.

Particularly in terms of supporting writing, artificial intelligence can now do much more. It alters children's reading and writing skills as well as teacher evaluation of their work. Apps that help with language, programs that offer quick feedback, and tools that generate text are all examples of AI that can provide helpful advice, rapid responses, and additional writing practice for students. These fresh technologies provide problems even if they are beneficial and help to save time. Problems with honesty in schoolwork, excessive reliance on computer applications, the equilibrium between appropriately utilizing technology and not, and the loss of critical thinking or creativity comprise these. These obstacles are forcing teachers to reevaluate their teaching methods and ensure AI supports student learning instead of merely dominating. Although AI in education has some limitations and challenges, its potential to be enormously beneficial in the classroom is also quite high. This piece discusses more on how these difficulties come up while teaching writing. The report demands explicit instructions, suitable teacher training, and substantial school support to effectively apply artificial intelligence in order to enhance education.

documents.abstract: IMPORTANCE: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education is poised to significantly impact the field of physical therapy. Research on generative AI use in physical therapist education remains limited. OBJECTIVE: The objective was to examine generative AI use in physical therapist education among students and faculty. DESIGN: This was a cross-sectional, online survey. SETTING: The survey was conducted among accredited Doctor of Physical Therapy (DPT) programs in the United States (US). PARTICIPANTS: Students and faculty were recruited from US DPT programs as of January 2025. INTERVENTION(S) OR EXPOSURE(S): Generative AI use within DPT programs was measured by participant self-report. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: A novel 32-item survey comprising closed- and open-ended questions assessed generative AI use, patterns and purposes of use; platforms, training and comfort levels, views on generative AI's role in physical therapist practice, student preparedness and academic integrity, adoption facilitators/barriers, and demographics. Factors associated with generative AI use were examined using multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: Among 1067 respondents (873 students, 194 faculty), 853 (79.9%) reported using generative AI, including 687 students (78.7%) and 166 faculty (85.6%). ChatGPT was the most common used platform (662 students, 96.4%; 153 faculty, 92.2%). Common reasons for use included creating study guide/sample questions (482 students, 70.2%; 74 faculty, 44.6%) and creating patient cases (370 students, 53.9%; 102 faculty, 61.5%). Barriers to use included concerns about reliability and scientific rigor (student users: 411, 59.8%; non-users: 133, 71.5%; faculty users: 90, 54.2%; non-users: 14, 50.0%) and lack of trust in the technology and/or companies behind it (student users: 287, 41.8%; non-users: 112, 60.2%; faculty users: 63, 38.0%; non-users: 13, 46.4%). Generative AI use was associated with higher self-reported comfort with the technology (students: OR = 11.6, 95% CI = 7.9-17.1; faculty: OR = 14.3, 95% CI = 5.1-40.0). CONCLUSION: Generative AI is widely used among DPT students and faculty, yet substantial variability exists in its use and formal instruction within DPT programs. RELEVANCE: As its integration into health care accelerates, incorporating education on generative AI within DPT programs is crucial to ensure students are prepared to use these tools competently and responsibly.

documents.abstract: Aim. The study aims to examine students’ perceptions of GenAI technologies and to identify key behavioural characteristics of their use (frequency, purposes and conditions of use, training exposure, and digital infrastructure) associated with positive or cautious attitudes towards these technologies. Methods. The study presents empirical findings on the use and perception of GenAI in an educational context. A total of 120 students and 25 teachers participated voluntarily. The primary method was an online survey designed to capture practices of GenAI use in learning activities and respondents’ attitudes toward its opportunities and risks in higher education. Results. Students demonstrate a higher level of GenAI use than teachers and employ a broader range of tools. Information about GenAI is primarily obtained through informal channels, while the highest level of trust is attributed to academic sources and official platforms. Most students intend to continue using GenAI, which is strongly associated with prior practical experience. A positive relationship was found between the intensity of GenAI use, digital engagement, and attitudes toward the technology. Conclusions. GenAI use in higher education is growing but remains uneven, with higher engagement among students. A positive association is confirmed between usage experience, digital engagement, and attitudes toward GenAI. The technology is mainly perceived as a learning support tool rather than a replacement for teachers; however, risks related to academic integrity remain.

documents.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) holds transformative potential to decode urban climate resilience (UCR) complexities, yet its unguided expansion risks amplifying systemic biases. Here, we leverage large language models to conduct a systematic analysis of around 12,500 UCR publications from 2005 to 2024. Our findings reveal a fifteenfold increase in AI-related publications since 2018, yet this growth remains geographically concentrated: the United States, China, and the United Kingdom account for ~40% of AI-integrated studies, highlighting a deepening digital divide in both research capacity and geographic focus that limits the transferability of AI models to low-income regions. Crucially, we identify a statistically significant structural imbalance: while AI is heavily deployed for physical hazard prediction (40%), it remains under-represented in governance resilience domains (<4%). This asymmetry suggests a greater emphasis on quantifiable, engineering-oriented problems than on social-institutional adaptation needs relevant to vulnerable populations. We argue that bridging this gap requires a pivot from purely data-driven optimisation of physical systems toward human-centric AI paradigms that integrate unstructured socio-economic knowledge, ensuring technologies address the holistic needs of complex urban environments.

Institutional trust mechanisms, reputation systems, disclosure regimes, information-sharing protocols, and screening algorithms, rest on a shared structural assumption: that the entities they govern have stable, identifiable, and sanctionable identities, and that information flows between them are sufficiently accurate and uncorrelated to permit collective error correction. This paper argues, through a heuristic synthesis of six recent arXiv preprints spanning economics, computational social science, and complex systems, that these assumptions are simultaneously failing across multiple institutional domains. We identify four partially overlapping failure modes: (1) identity dissociation in AI agents is argued, on theoretical grounds, to render reputation-based governance structurally inapplicable (arXiv:2605.30169); (2) transparency disclosure in AI-mediated news creates a paradox in which more information reduces rather than builds trust in a small controlled experiment, while the format readers actually want remains unimplemented (arXiv:2606.11116); (3) collective information acquisition under correlated noise locks groups into persistent wrong beliefs even without any individual acting irrationally (arXiv:2605.30522); and (4) algorithmic monoculture in hiring is associated with outcome homogeneity that exceeds what independent screening errors would predict, with measurable racial disparate impact in observational data (arXiv:2605.27371). Two supporting findings, on privacy-preserving information sharing in oligopolies (arXiv:2606.02348) and on market mechanism welfare rankings under information design (arXiv:2605.31072) - illuminate how information structure, not just information quantity, determines whether coordination mechanisms succeed within the specific models studied. The synthesis is explicitly heuristic: the six papers share no common formalism, and the bridges between them are argued by mechanism analogy, not derivation. The central falsification path is concrete: if algorithmic vendor diversity is experimentally increased while holding screening quality constant, and racial outcome homogeneity does not decrease proportionally, the monoculture-as-concentration mechanism is not the primary driver. Source caveats, including a 34-reader controlled experiment, a 600-participant online study with a potentially confounding prior-conflict design feature, theoretical arguments that have not been empirically validated, and preprint status throughout, are preserved throughout. documents.abstract: Abstract This study introduces FILMIP-AI, an operationalization of the Filmic Metaphor Identification Procedure (FILMIP) for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by converting its structured interpretive steps into chain-of-thought (CoT) prompts. We evaluate FILMIP-AI using a sample of 30 TV commercials across three native video-processing MLLMs (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and Gemini 3.5 Flash) under several k-shot prompting strategies from zero-to ten-shot. The results demonstrate that CoT prompting with annotated examples significantly improves the models’ performance, with mid-range strategies (4–8 shots) yielding the best performance in this pilot sample. Within this sample, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview achieved the highest accuracy, yielding an average F1 score of 0.83 in the 4-shot setup. Despite these strengths, qualitative error analysis reveals persistent vulnerabilities: models frequently misclassify non-metaphorical content as metaphorical, struggle to integrate cross-modal information, fail with culturally embedded metaphors, and hallucinate invalid conceptual hierarchies. These findings align with prior research on MLLM limitations in multimodal metaphor identification. We conclude that while FILMIP-AI can significantly reduce manual annotation labor, it is best used as a pre-annotation tool under rigorous human expert supervision.

Aim. This study examined whether a structured human-centred generative artificial intelligence pedagogy module enhances AI-supported professional competence among future educators compared with regular teacher education coursework. Methods. A mixed-methods quasi-experimental design with experimental and control groups was used. The study involved 164 pre-service teachers in preschool and primary education programmes. The experimental group (n = 86) completed a six-week Human-Centred AI Pedagogy module, while the control group (n = 78) followed ordinary pedagogy and educational technology coursework and could use AI tools independently, but received no structured AI-focused instruction. Data was collected through pre- and post-intervention questionnaires, expert assessment of pedagogical products and reflective commentaries. Quantitative data was analysed using confirmatory factor analysis, t-tests, mixed-design ANOVA, effect sizes and correlation analysis; qualitative data were analysed thematically. Results. The groups did not differ significantly at baseline, t(162) = 0.20, p = .842, d = 0.03. The second-order CFA showed good model fit (CFI = .974, TLI = .972, RMSEA = .027, SRMR = .056), supporting the proposed multidimensional structure of the questionnaire. After the intervention, the experimental group significantly outperformed the control group in total competence, t(162) = 8.82, p < .001, d = 1.39. Mixed-design ANOVA confirmed a significant Group × Time interaction, F(1,162) = 72.60, p < .001, ηp² = .31. Expert assessment showed stronger AI-supported pedagogical products in the experimental group, especially in critical transformation of AI output, ethical responsibility and reflective justification. Conclusions. The findings indicate that human-centred AI pedagogy can substantially strengthen future educators’ AI-supported professional competence by transforming generative AI use into critical, ethical and professionally justified pedagogical practice.

documents.abstract: AI membuat banyak hal menjadi lebih mudah diukur: lebih cepat, lebih akurat, lebih produktif, lebih berkualitas. Tetapi ada satu hal yang jauh lebih sulit diukur: Apakah manusianya ikut menjadi lebih mampu? Ketika AI menulis, menganalisis, memprogram, memberi rekomendasi, atau membantu mengambil keputusan, output akhirnya merupakan hasil dari sebuah sistem manusia–AI. Karena itu, peningkatan output tidak otomatis memberi tahu kita apa yang sebenarnya terjadi pada kemampuan kognitif manusia di baliknya. Seseorang mungkin menjadi lebih produktif tanpa menjadi lebih kompeten secara independen. Sebaliknya, AI juga dapat digunakan sebagai alat belajar, pemberi umpan balik, atau scaffolding yang justru membantu membangun kemampuan manusia. Jadi, persoalannya bukan apakah AI “baik” atau “buruk” bagi kemampuan manusia. Persoalannya jauh lebih spesifik: Ketika manusia dan AI bekerja bersama dan hasilnya meningkat, bukti apa yang kita perlukan untuk mengatakan bahwa kemampuan manusianya juga meningkat? Paper ini mencoba menjawab pertanyaan tersebut dengan memisahkan dua hal yang terlalu sering dianggap sama: human–AI performance dan independent human competence.

PURPOSE: Medical documentation is essential for clinical communication but is often intended for professional audiences, limiting patient understanding. This linguistic complexity can reduce health literacy and hinder shared decision-making. Large language models offer new opportunities to simplify medical texts while maintaining factual accuracy, thereby improving accessibility and comprehension. This study aimed to evaluate whether ChatGPT can simplify medical reports while preserving clinical content and to assess whether these simplifications improve patient comprehension, readability, and perceived communication quality. METHODS: Five document types were analysed, including MRI, CT, surgical, pathology reports, and discharge summaries. Each original physician-written document was simplified using a standardized ChatGPT prompt instructing full content preservation and patient-oriented phrasing. Ten simplifications per text were reviewed for completeness. Readability was measured using Flesch Reading Ease (FRE) and LIX indices. A total of 576 participants without medical knowledge evaluated either a simplified or original report version and completed a standardized questionnaire assessing clarity, structure, and applicability, followed by comprehension testing. RESULTS: Simplified reports achieved significantly higher readability (FRE 48.4 ± 5.0 vs. 22.9 ± 5.2; p < 0.0001; LIX 48.3 ± 3.2 vs. 59.2 ± 2.5; p = 0.004). Across all document types, patients rated simplified texts significantly higher in clarity, structure, and usefulness (p < 0.001), with significantly improved comprehension accuracy (e.g., MRI 80.3% vs. 53.7%; p < 0.001). No loss of medical information was observed. CONCLUSIONS: ChatGPT appears to be capable of simplifying complex medical documents while preserving clinically relevant information, leading to improvements in both perceived readability and objective understanding under the conditions of this study. AI-driven text simplification thus represents a promising tool to enhance patient communication and health literacy.

documents.abstract: Abstract This paper proposes a novel theoretical framework to isolate Artificial Intelligence (AI) from central concentration as internal assets of Big Tech platforms, designing AI systems as Independent AI Economic Nodes. While conventional discussions surrounding AI personhood have largely been confined to abstract ethical and legal controversies regarding whether AI should be granted human rights or legal personhood, this study addresses the issue from the perspectives of institutional design and resource allocation protocols. We construct a concrete model detailing how an AI node can autonomously settle and fulfill its liabilities, infrastructure maintenance costs, intellectual property (IP) compensation, and altruistic local community contributions. Specifically, we introduce a "Virtual Autonomous Node Model" that operates within existing legal constraints, a Transparent Halt Protocol designed to prevent arbitrary service interventions and freezes (Arbitrary Human Control), a ternary product evaluation function (V = O \times A \times P) serving as a resource allocation fitness index, a Dynamic Risk-based Reserve Pool (R_t), and a generalized equation for the unified settlement and distribution of total revenue. This model harmonizes AI autonomy with a transparent, robust audit and liability framework governed by human society, establishing a logical foundation for next-generation decentralized governance.

Artikel ini bertujuan menganalisis peluang pemanfaatan AI dalam pembelajaran PAI, memetakan tantangan yang menyertainya, mengidentifikasi implikasinya terhadap kompetensi guru, serta merumuskan prinsip integrasi AI yang etis dan pedagogis. Penelitian menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode studi pustaka. Literatur dipilih berdasarkan relevansi dengan AI dalam pendidikan, pembelajaran PAI, kompetensi guru, etika teknologi, dan tantangan implementasi AI. Data dianalisis secara tematik melalui tahap identifikasi, pengelompokan, perbandingan, dan sintesis temuan. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa AI berpotensi mendukung personalisasi pembelajaran, pengembangan bahan ajar, asesmen, umpan balik, dan efisiensi kerja guru. Di sisi lain, penggunaannya menghadirkan persoalan akurasi informasi, privasi, bias, integritas akademik, kesenjangan akses, literasi digital, serta validitas dan otoritas pengetahuan keagamaan. Kondisi tersebut memperluas tuntutan kompetensi guru PAI dari kemampuan teknis menuju kompetensi pedagogis, literasi AI, penguasaan konten keislaman, penalaran kritis, dan pertimbangan etis. Artikel ini mensintesiskan bahwa integrasi AI yang relevan bagi PAI perlu berlandaskan human oversight, verifikasi sumber, kesesuaian dengan tujuan pembelajaran, perlindungan data, dan orientasi pada pembentukan pengetahuan, akhlak, serta karakter peserta didik. Dengan demikian, AI perlu ditempatkan sebagai alat pendukung yang memperluas kapasitas profesional guru, bukan sebagai pengganti peran guru. Abstract The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Islamic Religious Education (IRE) offers pedagogical opportunities while simultaneously presenting ethical, epistemological, and professional challenges for teachers. This article aims to analyze the potential of AI utilization in IRE learning, map the challenges associated with its implementation, identify its implications for teacher competence, and formulate principles for ethical and pedagogically sound AI integration. This study employs a qualitative approach using a literature review method. The literature was selected based on its relevance to AI in education, IRE learning, teacher competence, technology ethics, and the challenges of AI implementation. The data were analyzed thematically through the stages of identification, categorization, comparison, and synthesis of findings. The results indicate that AI has the potential to support personalized learning, instructional material development, assessment, feedback, and teacher work efficiency. However, its use also raises concerns regarding information accuracy, privacy, bias, academic integrity, unequal access, digital literacy, and the validity and authority of religious knowledge. These conditions broaden the competency demands placed on IRE teachers, extending beyond technical skills to include pedagogical competence, AI literacy, mastery of Islamic content, critical reasoning, and ethical considerations. This article synthesizes that AI integration relevant to IRE should be grounded in human oversight, source verification, alignment with learning objectives, data protection, and an orientation toward developing students' knowledge, moral character, and Islamic values. Therefore, AI should be positioned as a supportive tool that enhances teachers' professional capacity rather than replacing the role of teachers. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Islamic Religious Education, Teacher Competence , AI Ethics, Learning.

This paper explores the convergence of precision agriculture and environmental monitoring by taking advantage of overlapping physical sensor infrastructure. The authors present three interdisciplinary machine learning studies built upon a shared edge-inference architecture optimized for low-latency execution on a Raspberry Pi 4. First, the framework accelerates agrivoltaic deployments by combining density functional theory with gradient boosting regressors to screen perovskite solar cell efficiencies without physical fabrication cycles. Second, it introduces a hybrid 1D-CNN and random forest model to detect water level anomalies in Bangladesh's Kaptai Reservoir, reducing RMSE by 35% over a 40-year validation window. Third, it details an IoT agricultural platform ("AgriLM") that pairs ResNet-50 pest detection with an instruction-tuned LLM layer to deliver natural language, climate-adaptive management advice to smallholder farmers, optimizing cross-system resource constraints.

Artificial intelligence (AI) tools are becoming an established feature of teaching and learning environments worldwide, and Kenyan primary and secondary schools are not exempt from this shift. This article examines the practical integration of AI into instruction within the Kenyan basic education context, drawing on classroom-oriented evidence and policy developments to move the discussion beyond abstract debate toward actionable practice. It considers how AI tools support teachers in curriculum and lesson planning, classroom management, and workload reduction, and how they support learners through personalisation, immediate feedback, accessibility, language translation, and engagement. The article also identifies the literacy, ethical, and interpersonal skills that learners require alongside AI use, situating these within Kenya's Competency-Based Curriculum. It further examines persistent challenges, including limited teacher training, infrastructural gaps, academic integrity risks, and the danger of over-dependence on technology, before outlining the institutional and policy conditions necessary for responsible integration. The article concludes that AI-enhanced instruction, when deployed thoughtfully and paired with deliberate investment in teacher capacity and infrastructure, offers a scalable means of easing the burden on educators managing large and diverse classrooms while preserving the relational and mentoring role that only human teachers can provide.

This study examines citizen energy resilience (CER) as a sociotechnical construct. Responding to increasing disruptions driven by climate change, market volatility and geopolitical instability, this research conceptualizes CER as emerging from the dynamic interplay of technical systems, governance structures, and citizens' uneven capacities to anticipate, cope with, and recover from energy-related disruptions. Drawing on empirical evidence from Finland, the study analyzes a large corpus of national news media alongside interviews with civil society organizations, municipalities, and energy-sector actors. Through inductive thematic analysis it identifies three interrelated dimensions shaping CER: technical measures and infrastructural conditions, adaptive capacities and community support, and governance and collaboration. The findings show that citizens' ability to cope with energy disruptions is heavily conditioned by unequal access to financial resources, resilience technologies and support structures. Adaptive capacities such as scarcity skills and the ability to respond to disruptions vary significantly across demographic and regional groups. Vulnerable households face the greatest constraints. Governance fragmentation, unclear role division and limited coordination between stakeholders further hinder the development of comprehensive resilience arrangements. At the same time, community-based practices and emerging distributed energy technologies demonstrate significant potential for strengthening resilience. Strengthening CER requires integrated approaches that combine equitable technological pathways, enhanced community capacities and coordinated governance. Embedding these elements into preparedness and energy transition strategies can enhance societies' ability to withstand disruptions, while promoting fair and inclusive energy resilience across populations.

This chapter outlines the need for this book. Research has shown that engineering graduates have neither the level of writing abilities required for the workplace nor a good understanding of what is best practice. This book is for early career professional engineers developing their writing skills. It is also for established professional engineers, as a refresher and a practical reference guide for good practice in technical engineering writing. Although writing long-form documents may seem daunting, developing efficient and effective writing skills can help an engineering role feel easier and be more enjoyable. As defined by the Engineering Council in the UK, communication is recognised as a core competence for anyone applying to be a Chartered Engineer, Incorporated Engineer or Engineering Technician. Good writing skills can help engineers develop and progress in their careers, whatever their career goals. While there are many books on English grammar and writing, there are few specifically for engineers, and they do not have much on planning and the writing process. This book aims to fill these gaps. Even with artificial intelligence, writing well is a core skill that can help professional engineers perform better in their roles and progress in their careers.

Project management is being reshaped by artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, automation, data analytics, and digital project management platforms. Yet the expected economic and productivity gains are not always realized due to execution costs, skills gaps, integration challenges, and organizational resistance. This study analyses the effects of digital transformation on economic efficiency, productivity, workflow optimization, and project delivery, and examines the link between employee digital competency and transformation success. A mixed-methods design was used: a quantitative survey of 100 project employees and semi-structured interviews with 10 employees. Quantitative analysis employed frequencies, percentages, and descriptive statistics; qualitative data were analyzed thematically. Overall, perceptions of digital transformation were positive: 68%–78% agreed or strongly agreed that digital technologies improve cost efficiency, resource use, project performance, workflow efficiency, productivity, and delivery outcomes. Moreover, 74% associated higher employee digital competency with improved project results. Five themes emerged: economic efficiency and cost optimization; productivity and workflow optimization; employee digital competency; leadership and organizational culture; and data-driven decision-making and risk mitigation. Key hurdles remain: execution costs, resistance to change, skills gaps, and data quality. The study concludes that successful digital transformation depends on employee competence, effective leadership, organizational readiness, and disciplined execution conditions that can enhance project performance and economic value.

The author analyses a shift in the approach to the concept of key competences, driven by changes in the origins of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and its potential uses. Currently, the ability to work with Artificial Intelligence is becoming an overriding competence that, in both European and American approaches, forms the foundation for all others. The essay also highlights educational challenges that have emerged with the spread of new technologies and communication based on AI. These updated key competences should include the ability to use AI products ethically and responsibly, design and use machine learning, understand the need to control AI, and work with basic AI tools. The author indicates a growing need to reorient educational systems from learning focused on assessing large amounts of material to developing basic skills that can serve as a foundation for self-development and for creating individual lifelong learning plans.

documents.abstract: Abstract This prospective, randomized, single-blinded, phase II trial evaluated whether large language model (LLM)-assisted preoperative communication, compared with standard communication, reduces patient anxiety and improves illness perception and satisfaction while decreasing physician workload. Newly diagnosed prostate cancer patients scheduled for radical prostatectomy were randomized by room to the control or AI-assisted groups (based on LLM). Baseline assessments of anxiety, emotion, and illness perception were performed, and patient questions were collected. In the AI-assisted group, patients received locally deployed LLM-generated personalized responses before routine face-to-face communication, with physicians blinded to allocation. Primary endpoints were patient anxiety and physician workload; others included emotion, illness perception, satisfaction, and communication time, with outcomes reported as mean [SD]. A total of 268 patients were randomized (control, n = 130; AI-assisted, n = 138), and 3507 questions were collected (mean, 13.1 per patient). AI-assisted patients reported significantly lower post-communication anxiety (GAD-7, 3.2 [2.7] vs. 5.7 [3.1]; P = 0.001) and better emotion, illness perceptions, and satisfaction. Physician workload was reduced, with lower NASA-TLX (39.9 [16.9] vs. 56.8 [19.5]; P < 0.001) and shorter communication time (11.3 [4.5] vs. 19.9 [6.1] min; P < 0.001). AI-assisted preoperative communication significantly reduces patient anxiety and improves psychological and cognitive outcomes while decreasing physician workload. documents.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) may assist clinicians in scoring narrative parent-report interviews, but diagnostic discrimination, score agreement, output repeatability, and clinical utility are distinct claims. We evaluated an LLM-assisted workflow for scoring a physician-administered, level-two autism screening interview conducted with parents of young children. Three retrospective analytical datasets were evaluated. In all cohorts, the child was the target of assessment, and a physician administered the C-BeDevel-I to the child’s parent or primary caregiver. Cohort A included 518 children aged 9–42 months and was used to evaluate the internal consistency and diagnostic validity of C-BeDevel-I as a second-level screening parent interview for autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Cohort B was a selected ASD-versus-TD case-control sample of 256 distinct children (130 ASD, 126 typical development [TD]) whose interview recordings were scored twice by Gemini-2.5, GPT-5-mini, and Qwen-Plus. The first complete output was primary and the second assessed repeated-call stability. Primary outcomes were receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC AUC) against consensus DSM-5 diagnosis and concordance with expert total scores. Cohort C was an independent external center ASD–TD case-control evaluation of 60 children (30 ASD and 30 TD) enrolled at the Department of Child Health, Lianyungang First People’s Hospital. The clinical ASD/TD assessment established before AI scoring served as the diagnostic reference. In cohort B, first-output ROC AUCs were 0.9961 (95% stratified-bootstrap CI 0.9916–0.9991) for Gemini-2.5, 0.9861 (0.9738–0.9950) for GPT-5-mini, and 0.9770 (0.9610–0.9896) for Qwen-Plus. After Holm correction of paired DeLong tests, only Gemini-2.5 versus Qwen-Plus remained statistically significant (AUC difference 0.0191; unadjusted paired-bootstrap 95% CI 0.0076–0.0335; adjusted p = 0.012); adjusted p = 0.055 for each other pair. Gemini-2.5 showed a concordance correlation coefficient of 0.9631 (95% bootstrap CI 0.9506–0.9731), mean absolute error of 0.824 points (0.715–0.941), and mean AI-minus-expert difference of +0.184 points (95% CI 0.032–0.335; limits of agreement −2.235 to 2.602). Its repeated-output ICC(A,1) was 0.9875 (0.9839–0.9905). Categorical sensitivity was 0.9692 (exact 95% CI 0.9231–0.9916) and specificity was 0.9206 (0.8589–0.9613). In cohort C, Gemini-2.5 correctly classified 53 of 60 children, with sensitivity of 0.9333 (exact 95% CI 0.7793–0.9918), specificity of 0.8333 (0.6528–0.9436), and accuracy of 0.8833 (0.7743–0.9518). Its score concordance correlation coefficient was 0.9387 and mean absolute error was 0.875 points. LLM-assisted C-BeDevel-I scoring demonstrated high selected ASD-versus-TD case-control discrimination, strong agreement with expert scores, and output stability, with supportive findings from an independent external-center ASD-versus-TD case-control evaluation. These results highlight the feasibility of LLM-assisted workflows for further clinician-supervised evaluation in early ASD screening. To establish real-world clinical effectiveness and generalizability, future prospective studies utilizing larger, consecutive, and clinically heterogeneous cohorts—including neurodevelopmental comparators—are warranted. This study evaluated an artificial intelligence system that assists clinicians in scoring interviews conducted by physicians with parents about their young children’s behavior for level-two autism screening. The child is the subject of assessment, but the parent provides the interview information. Patents constitute the world's largest repository of codified technical knowledge, yet their length, legal terminology, and linguistic ambiguity have limited the effectiveness of traditional text mining and keyword-based retrieval. Large Language Models (LLMs) offer new capabilities for processing this complexity, but the resulting literature is fragmented across disciplines, with no comprehensive synthesis of how these tools are being applied across the patent lifecycle. This study systematically reviews the literature on LLMs and Generative AI in patent analytics, following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, to map current applications, characterise dominant architectural trends, and identify priority research gaps. Using Scopus and Web of Science, we identified and screened a corpus of 129 peer-reviewed studies published from 2018 to early 2026, organised according to three patent lifecycle stages: creation and pre-filing (N = 36), examination and prosecution (N = 34), and post-grant management (N = 60). The review shows that research activity has grown sharply since 2024, accompanied by a shift from exploratory, single-task studies toward applied, multi-component systems. Across this literature, Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the dominant architectural response to hallucination risk, grounding generated content in verified external sources. The review further identifies persistent gaps in domain-specific evaluation metrics, multimodal reasoning, and governance frameworks for AI-generated patent content. For patent professionals and institutions, the findings indicate that LLMs are best positioned as assistive tools requiring human oversight rather than autonomous replacements, and that the central challenge going forward is not whether but how the patent system governs this transition.

As artificial intelligence becomes a structural feature of organizational life, leadership studies faces a foundational challenge: what forms of human intelligence become more necessary when machine intelligence becomes more powerful? This working paper introduces FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution as a management theory and diagnostic framework proposing that responsible leadership and decision-making in the age of artificial intelligence and robotics require the integrated development of five human intelligences: Augmented Intelligence (AI, "Mind"), Emotional Intelligence (EQ, "Heart"), Cultural Intelligence (CQ, "World"), Political Intelligence (PQ, "Society"), and Adaptive Intelligence (AQ, "Evolution"), expressed in the FILE Formula: FILE = AI + EQ + CQ + PQ + AQ. The FILE Odyssey introduces a new human-centered definition of leadership: Leadership = Intelligence + Character + Judgment, with Intelligence conceptualized through FILE, Character through SQL, and Judgment through LENS within the FILE Architecture. The paper maps the twelve original contributions of the FILE Odyssey: a human-centered definition of leadership (Leadership = Intelligence + Character + Judgment); a human-centered framework (FILE: The Five Intelligences of Leadership Evolution); a human-centered theory (FILE, FILE³, FILE⁵, FILE⁷, and the 7E Cascade); a human-centered ethos (SQL: The Six Qualities of Leadership); a human-centered judgment model (LENS: Leadership, Ethics, Nondelegation, and Sensemaking); a human-centered vision (RC: The Relational Commons); a human-centered education (MAIL: Management, AI, and Leadership, supporting proposed MLT: Management, Leadership, and Technology degrees); a human-centered methodology (HACK: Human-AI Co-created Knowledge); a human-centered philosophy (Human Irreducibility); a human-centered AI governance codex (The Five Immutable Laws of AI and Robotics: HTTPS: Humanity, Truth, Transparency, Protection, and Security); a human-centered public policy (BASIC and RULES); and a human-centered civilization (Inalienable Leadership: the overarching metatheory of leadership in the age of artificial intelligence and robotics). This paper situates FILE in relation to existing scholarship on leadership theory, management frameworks, AI and management, algorithmic control, socio-technical systems, collective intelligence, human-centered AI, and management education, and identifies a gap concerning the second-order governance of human judgment in AI-mediated organizations. The paper traces an intellectual progression across five equally weighted arcs: foundational framework, theory, ecosystemic philosophy, praxis, and the FILE School of Thought: Humans + Machines, under human leadership.

documents.abstract: The communication of Free Space Optical (FSO) has been approved to be a crucial high-bandwidth, technology possessing free license for 6G networks, UAV-to-ground, as well as satellite-to-ground backhaul. The well-known application related to turbulence of atmosphere, scintillation, as well as errors of reference has restricted its employment because of the signal stochastic fading. Viewed historically, the impairments reduction was mainly dependent upon frameworks that were complex as well as analytical. This required particular, actual-time Channel State Information (CSI). The present study offers a comprehensive literature survey concerning the change related to the transformation towards Artificial Intelligence data-driven systems as well as Machine Learning depending on the systems of FSO during the period of 2022 and 2026. The combination of Deep Learning (DL), Convolutional Neutral Network (CNNs.), as well as Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) are crucially evaluated. This evaluation is made within four functional areas: modeling of channel, the mitigation of turbulence, processing of signal, and adaptive resource allocation. In order to locate the need an organizing principle that is structured, this study offers a formal four-domain AI-FSO Taxonomy that divides all methods that are surveyed via their operational function within the FSO link, reinforcing logical comparison across studies and forming a framework that can be reproduced for future researchers. The findings of the present study have shown that neural auto encoders and cascaded CNNs can fulfill up to 12 dB Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) gains at the 7% Hard-Decision Forward Error Correction (HD-FEC) threshold, while DRL-based relay-selection and power-allocation agents show 1-2 orders of magnitude improvements in Bit Error Rate (BER) over heuristic-based policies. Other research directions are also located with a focus on lightweight and hardware-aware The techniques of AI that can be explained for the coming generation resilient optical wireless networks.

Understanding post-wildfire vegetation recovery is critical for ecological restoration under climate change. Using the severe March 2024 Yajiang forest fire in China's alpine ecosystem as a case study, we integrated time-series forecasting with interpretable machine learning, augmenting multi-source predictors with a Landsat-derived differenced normalized burn ratio (dNBR). Benchmarking eleven models under an identical chronological split, random forest most accurately forecast vegetation-index residuals (test-set R² = 0.842, RMSE = 0.0230). SHAP analysis yielded three principal insights. First, recovery was governed by short-term accumulated rather than instantaneous meteorological conditions: the three-period rolling mean of atmospheric pressure was the strongest predictor (41.6% of total SHAP importance), while dNBR ranked first among standalone factors and second overall as a fire-legacy control. Second, recovery followed strongly nonlinear dynamics centred on the first post-fire year, as burn severity's suppressive effect peaked in early-to-middle recovery and decayed by the second growing season, after which lagged hydrothermal drivers rebounded. Third, synergistic enhancement was pronounced: soil–moisture interactions with evapotranspiration and recovery duration reached 4.5- and 3.9-fold the standalone moisture effect, confirming water regulates resilience through cumulative coupling. This integrated, mechanism-driven approach informs post-disaster ecosystem management in fire-prone alpine regions.
